about.title: Ferndale Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Ferndale is home to roughly 1,369 people, and in a place that size, losing a family member is never a private event. Neighbors on Main Street notice. Coworkers notice. The house feels different. What most families do not have room to think about in those first weeks is whether someone else's carelessness caused the loss, and whether California law gives them any recourse. It often does. A wrongful death claim is a civil action, entirely separate from any criminal charge, brought by the people closest to the person who died. In Ferndale, the most recent final year on record, 2025, logged no injury collisions and no traffic deaths inside city limits, which is genuinely good news. Yet fatal harm still reaches local families through crashes elsewhere in Humboldt County, medical errors, workplace incidents, or hazards on someone's property. The collision reports that do exist here cluster along Bluff Street, Main Street, and Fairview Drive, mostly on Thursday evenings. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that matches you with an independent attorney who handles wrongful death cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.
commonInjuries: Fatal motor vehicle collisions on county roads and highways
Pedestrian or bicyclist deaths involving a driver
Deaths tied to medical or nursing home negligence
Falls or hazards on unsafe property

whyChoose.title: Why Ferndale Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: We help sort out who can file
items.desc: California limits standing to a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can confirm where your family fits before anything is filed.

items.title: Deadlines get watched from day one
items.desc: Most claims must be brought within two years of the date of death, and far sooner when a government entity is involved. Connecting early keeps those windows open.

items.title: Every category of loss is considered
items.desc: Recoverable damages can include funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. The attorneys in our network build claims around all of it, on contingency.

items.question: Ferndale reported no traffic deaths in 2025. Can a wrongful death case still involve someone from here?
items.answer: Yes. Those figures count only collisions inside city limits, and Ferndale residents drive, work, and receive medical care throughout Humboldt County and beyond. A death that happened on a rural road outside town, in a hospital, or on a job site can still support a claim brought by family members living here.

items.question: The other person is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death lawsuit is a civil matter and proceeds on its own track, regardless of whether prosecutors file charges or how a criminal case ends. Waiting can actually work against you, because the two-year civil deadline keeps running the whole time.

items.question: What does using LawProactive cost a grieving family?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm, and the independent attorneys we match you with work on contingency. That means no fee unless there is a recovery, so you can ask questions without adding another bill to an already heavy month.
